title: I'm working on a tool for ai character animation
author: melonboy55
selftext:
So I quit my job 4 months ago and I've just been working on this thing non stop. 

It's a tool for animating characters. It takes a character through a workflow of pose => motion => spritesheet using models that are trained for that specific task.  
  
Currently all I have built are simple sidescroller motions for 'walk', 'run', 'jump', 'punch', 'fall down', 'get up'.  
It keeps character consistency pretty well. But it's not perfect. There's lots of little issues with it, but I'm making progress! I'm excited to share it with ya'll soon!

I recon that will make or break your product.

replies.author: melonboy55
replies.body:
I agree, that seems really important. Ideally the models i train understand when it's supposed to be a loop. (all their training data is looped) but in practice they don't always nail it.  
I'm also working on tooling to make frame selection and editing much easier. Video => sprite sheet should be as flexible as you need it to be.  
There are also open souce workflows that let you 'insert' new frames in the middle of a video (or at the end). very cool stuff. I think that could be useful for getting the loops right like you are talking about.   
There is a lot of work to do!

replies.author: melonboy55
replies.body:
do you mean like resolution? I've set some arbitrary limits but I'm open to changing that if people really want to make giant sprites.

The default video resolution is 512x512 (for speed), which then makes a spritesheet where each sprite is 512x512.   
There's also a hard upload cap at 6MB for images and 12MB for videos.

I've also forced everything to square aspect ratio (1:1). not for any real reason i just thought it was easier to think about.  
  
Do you need really big sprites? I hadn't really thought about it before

replies.author: Exarch92
replies.body: Yeah exactly, dimensions! Ah sweet that would fit my use case perfectly!

replies.author: melonboy55
replies.body:
hmmm!! you bring up some good points. This is something that I'm not as familiar with. Right now in the app you can set sprite sheet fps when you create it from a video.  
  
Do you think people would want sprite sheets that span multiple sheets? I could set a hard resolution cap per sheet, or i could just always generate a single sheet no matter what size it is. (the most you could ever have is 81 frames, 16fps x  5 seconds)  
  
Would it be more useful if you could customize it? set frames per sheet or max size or something?

replies.author: Exarch92
replies.body:
hmm i do think that configuring that would be a positive addition. i believe it boils down to how smooth a developer would want the animations to be. the more sprites per sheet the smoother the animation. someone might want go for a more retro styled game where they might only want a few sprites per animation to make the animation "choppy"...

and then more modern games would need higher number of sprites per animation.

hmm that i really dont know, i guess it all comes down to how each implementation parses sprite data. i think any number of rows would work. :)
